chunks: Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a mukatab (slave under contract of emancipation) jointly owned by two partners, and one of them frees his share: How should the servant act? He said: "He serves the second partner one day and serves himself one day." I asked: "What if he dies and leaves wealth?" He said: "The wealth is divided equally between the one who freed his share and the one who retained his share."

key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has contracted with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a jointly-owned freed slave divided if he dies before completing his emancipation?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Sadiq clarifies the practical mechanics of a mukataba (contract of manumission) for a jointly owned slave, establishing a rotational service model where the slave alternates between serving the remaining partner and working for himself. The ruling ensures equitable debt settlement while preserving the ownership rights of the second partner, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in commercial and manumission contracts. In the event of the slave's death, the remaining capital is divided equally, highlighting the shared financial liability in such partnerships.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3473 - Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a mukatab (slave undera contract of emancipation) jointly owned by two partners, and one of them freed his share.

Imam (as) said: "The slave serves the second partner one day and serves himself one day."
I asked: "What if the slave dies and leaves behind wealth?"
Imam (as) said: "The wealth is divided equally between the one who freed his share and the one who retained his share."
